ARQUIMEA DEUTSCHLAND GmbH (ARQ-D) is a German private company with Headquarters in Frankfurt (Oder), devoted to design, development and commercialization of space-qualified parts, including microelectronics, electronics and mechanisms. 

ARQ-D is a fabless Design House specialized in radiation-hardened-by-design (RHBD) integrated circuits for space and other harsh environments such as nuclear, aviation or medical applications. ARQ-D’s devices are designed to be immune to electrical degradation produced by cumulated radiation dose or high energy particles. ARQ-D specializes in analog, digital and mixed-signal microelectronics, covering the full supply chain, from feasibility analysis and requirements review up to qualification according to Space standards (ESCC, NASA and MIL). The following capabilities can be highlighted:
-	Space-qualified ASIC/FPGA turnkey projects
-	Deep submicron (up to 65nm) analog, digital and mixed-signal design
-	IP cores design and integration
-	Standardized design methodologies
-	Process or device electrical and radiation characterization
-	Silicon evaluation 
-	Test chips design
-	Flight model validation

ARQUIMEA provides turnkey analog, digital and mixed-signal ASICs by covering the full supply chain, from the definition of the ASIC specification in collaboration with the user, up to the delivery of the qualified chip. This implies the establishment of a complete network of partnerships with reliable partners and suppliers for the different steps of the development and procurement of our integrated circuits.

ARQ-D is also commercial partner and exclusive distributor of space-qualified actuators and mechanisms using Shape Memory Alloys (SMA) belonging to its Sister Company ARQUIMEA INGENIERIA.

PRODEVELOP is specialized in consulting, development, deploying, and operating geospatial solutions based on free and open source software. The success in our projects is based on the acquired experience in geospatial industry, and the collaboration with the main developers groups in the world. entityDescription:
The University of Palermo is an internationally acknowledged public research organization which covers almost all main fields of study fostering an interdisciplinary approach. 
Its internationalization strategy envisaged in 2020 n. 53 double-degree study courses and 10 courses as well as 418 study subjects delivered in English. 
The University welcomes about 500 enrolled foreign students and 351 incoming ERASMUS students per year and is active in 186 international agreements for interuniversity cooperation.
The academic structures include: 16 Departments, 1 School of Medicine, 21 libraries, 3 decentralised premises (Agrigento, Trapani, Caltanissetta), the Museum System, the Language Centre, the Italian school for foreign students, the Guidance Centre.
The educational offer for the academic year 2021/2022 encompasses 144 degree courses (first and second cycle), 40 master courses, 29 specialization schools, 23 PhD programmes.
The academic community in 2020 consisted of 42.320 students, 1.468 lecturers, 81 research fellows, 685 PhDs, 1.255 students attending specialisation courses, 1.410 managers, technical and administrative staff units.
Research projects in operation in 2020 were 206.
In order to implement its third mission, the University of Palermo has set up an Industrial Liaison Office, launched a network of University labs (ATEN Center) for testing and transferring new technologies to SMEs, founded a university business incubator and started up a Contaminaton Lab. The University labs integrated system has been conceived to create synergies among the different academic skills available, enhance coordination with other centres and exploit research results to generate economic value.
The business incubator located within the University Campus of Palermo, managed by Consorzio ARCA (a public-private partnership) intends to boost the growth and success of innovative business ideas by means of a structured network of resources and services. It provides interdisciplinary entrepreneurship education training packages, helps generate profitable start-ups, supports academic spin-off companies and assists students for their participation in business plan competitions joined by the University
